title: Choose Setu’s visual world
question: Choose the system that should govern both the Penpot design system and the Kanban board.

options.label: Assembly Traveler Matrix
options.lineage: PCB assembly travelers and factory dispatch boards
options.thesis: Status and priority form a physical routing matrix while milestones travel through the board as copper traces.
options.viewport: A wide operating board fills the frame: status across the top, a fixed priority rail down the left, and milestone traces routing behind movable task slips.
options.risk: The manufacturing lineage can feel severe if functional labels drift into factory jargon.

raised.raise: One continuous geometry now drives both board structure and milestone routing.
Copper appears only on real actions and active drop targets.
Every state is named and patterned so color never carries status alone.
A move previews its destination and milestone impact before commitment.

options.label: Release Coordinate Plot
options.lineage: systems plotting tables and engineering control charts
options.thesis: The board behaves like a live coordinate plot: status is the x-axis, priority is the y-axis, and every task has one unambiguous position.
options.viewport: A precise axis-led board occupies nearly the whole screen, with a slim command rail and milestone paths drawn as measured overlays.
options.risk: It is the most familiar enterprise direction and can feel generic unless the coordinate logic governs every interaction.

options.label: Quoted Dispatch Floor
options.lineage: industrial streetwear labels and stockroom wayfinding
options.thesis: Literal quoted labels, hard black-and-white zones, and safety-orange dispatch tags make ownership and movement impossible to miss.
options.viewport: A stark full-width dispatch board uses oversized quoted status labels and one orange active-task tag crossing the matrix.
options.case: Strong audience recognition and decisive hierarchy; less calm than the assigned direction for an all-day operating surface.
options.risk: The quotation grammar and hazard stripes can become tiring when every region speaks at full volume.

options.label: One-Bit Project Desktop
options.thesis: The board becomes a crisp one-bit desktop where task windows, marching selections, and integer-pixel states make direct manipulation tangible.
options.viewport: A tiled Kanban window dominates the desktop while a compact milestone window overlaps its lower edge and the selected task wears marching ants.
options.case: High developer recognition and strong direct-manipulation character; milestone relationships are less immediately legible.
options.risk: Retro novelty can overpower readability at balanced task density.

options.label: Task Territory Map
options.thesis: Priority territories swell around tasks while milestone routes cross their coastlines.
options.viewport: One large priority territory fills the board with status destinations pinned along its coast.
options.case: The route metaphor is memorable but weakens the familiar Kanban scan pattern.
options.kept: One geometry drives layout, grouping, and milestone routing.
options.risk: Organic territories obscure exact row and column positions.

options.label: Warm Action Cards
options.thesis: Comfortable cards and a single action-only accent make every available move obvious.
options.viewport: A generous board of soft cards sits on a warm ground with one saturated move action visible.
options.case: Clear and usable, but it identifies with consumer apps rather than developer operations.
options.kept: Reserve saturated color strictly for actionable elements.
options.risk: The comfortable card language becomes indistinguishable from generic SaaS tooling.

options.label: Release Horizon
options.thesis: Status columns become named phases of light from backlog night to shipped day.
options.viewport: Tasks advance across horizontal light bands whose named phases brighten toward completion.
options.case: Phase progression is clear, but atmospheric light competes with task state and priority scanning.
options.kept: Name and pattern every phase so status is never color-only.
options.risk: The dramatic gradient field is too atmospheric for sustained daily operation.

options.label: Development Trays
options.thesis: Tasks develop through fixed stations with preview strips before a move commits.
options.viewport: A linear row of process trays holds cards that reveal more detail as they move toward completion.
options.case: Fixed stations map to status, but irreversible process conflicts with freely movable task planning.
options.kept: Preview the destination and side effects before committing a move.
options.risk: The dark amber environment reduces long-session clarity and misstates reversible movement.

canonCard.label: Polished SaaS Kanban
canonCard.thesis: A familiar neutral project board with equal status columns, white task cards, compact filters, and one blue-violet accent.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional project header sits above evenly divided columns filled with tidy cards and colored metadata pills.
canonCard.risk: Immediately usable but intentionally indistinguishable from established project-management products.
